body: A new layout engine version changes the computed layout of every document, remote pages included: every box position and size the engine reports may move, and the chunk must measure that change, not assume it away.

Floats are now placed under a caller-defined float id (#1303): the inline layout passes the node's taffy id when it places a floated box, so floated content's placement is a behaviour the take changes.

Bounds the snapshot and the accessibility tree report for a node, a closed select's options, an open list's rows and a multiple select's rows and groups are read from layout, so the move reaches every bound those readings carry.
The open select list's rows taking one height, and the shot of an open list's row, rest on layout the move may shift; their checks must still hold after the move.
Hit-testing and the driver's synthetic click at a node's centre, its covered-click refusal and a click in a shown scrollbar band read layout boxes; the move must leave those checks passing.
Content with display none stays out of the accessibility tree; the layout engine's handling of display none comes with the new Taffy and the exclusion must still hold.

The stand checks are re-run as part of the measurement: the stand's contrast assertions measured from computed styles, the stand reading no lint finding at boot, the shared focus-order table, all repeated three rounds.
The lint's contrast finding carries bounds read from layout; its bounds may move with the new layout and the finding's shape must stay as it stands.
The accessibility test leg in the slow tier and the accessibility checks that gate CI must stay green on the moved tree; a red leg with no in-scope fix is a stop for the phase.

Accessibility is a default-on feature and the session library always enables it: the build, clippy and doc legs measured on the moved tree are the feature-on builds, so the AccessKit tree's code path is compiled and checked under the new Taffy.

The lock may move only taffy and what the move forces: the AccessKit crates and the platform adapter the accessibility tree rests on take no version change the move does not force, and any such forced change is read in the measurement.
A hidpi or zoom change reshapes text and the viewport carries scheme and zoom; text and box layout read under the new Taffy at every zoom the stand checks use must still meet their checks.
Whether each layout change the chain brings is its own ratification, or the founder's Taffy-only lifting stands as the ruling for them, is a fork the measurement names and does not settle.
Role mapping by HTML-AAM, ARIA role, state and property reads, and accessible name precedence: they derive from attributes and elements, never from layout.
Keyboard handling rows: range input keys, select list key handling and its input and change events, Tab order and focus movement, keyboard activation; the move changes no key or focus logic.
The choice of AccessKit for the tree and of accesskit_xplat as platform adapter, the stand binaries building no adapter, and the adapter's creation order: the chunk changes no adapter or tree source.
Cognitive accessibility rows (invalid state not by colour or class alone): no layout or dependency reach.

Driver and MCP answer shapes: the actions answer, handler coverage, MCP tool results, the snapshot text form, the snapshot diff, served node id separator, the UI graph state registration and the Dioxus reached-handler record; the move adds or changes no field.
Password masking, the password caret and value reveal rules: untouched by a layout dependency move.

The incremental oracle invariant: one pipeline for incremental and full layout, both layout modes giving identical layouts, must hold on the moved Taffy.

body: The cargo legs run locked: every build, test and CI leg keeps its locked flag, and the moved lock must satisfy it with taffy from a git source.
The minimum supported Rust version 1.91, verified by build only: the git taffy and anything it pulls must build at 1.91, or the move stops.
The dependency audit over advisories and licences: a git taffy still passes it; any second git source the move would bring is a fork, not a fix.
Clippy over the workspace and upstream blitz-dom: the taffy move and the inline-layout call change must leave both clippy legs clean.
The workspace tested in the fast CI leg, and per-package green is not workspace green: the measurement reads the whole workspace's tests, not one crate's.
The incremental layout differential oracle: its invariant holds after the move; the move is re-measured against it, since the new taffy changes layout.
Layout assertions and stand checks run in both layout modes: a layout change brought by the new taffy is read in both modes, not one.
The stand checks on the bundled real font with no skip, and their zero-failure repeat budget: the move must leave them green under the same budget.

Floated box placement: Taffy #1303's caller-defined float id changes how inline layout hands a float to the block context; a test that pins float placement reads that the floats still place where they did, or names what moved.

Layout behaviour changes the chain brings change layout for every document, remote pages included; each one the measurement finds is named as a change (and as a fork on whether it needs its own ratification), and a test proving a changed layout documents what moved.
The WPT conformance runner must still build against the git taffy; its reading stays report-only, so a moved WPT score is measured and named, never a gate to fix.
The blitz-tests manifest's difference from upstream: the taffy source the tests build against follows the workspace's, and that difference is re-read rather than widened.
The local pre-push gate and host-reproducible CI legs: the measurement runs the same legs on the host in the trial worktree that CI runs.
Regression tests document and are named for their bug: any test the chunk adds for a layout the move breaks or fixes follows that rule.
Font-metric tests never skip and pixel tests stay on a CPU buffer: a layout move the new taffy brings is read through them as they stand, not by loosening them.

body_fields.convention: each new integration test of a layout behaviour sits in its own test target, one target per behaviour and per file
each new unit test sits in an inline test module in its source file
each new test's data is stated in code, its fixtures built without seeding, shared fixture pages stated once
each new test is shown red before green, and a table-driven test asserts its row count

body: The session lifecycle, its socket wire, host, state directory, errors and recording rows: the chunk changes no session code and no wire.
The MCP server, the escher-session command line, its exit codes, stderr and stdout lines: no command-line or MCP surface moves.
The cold-agent pipe, its events, verdict, exit codes and isolation: no cold-agent run is part of this chunk.
The agent-run verbs, selections, events and exit codes: the agent-run contract is untouched.
Driver refusal causes, driver verbs, snapshot nodes, element ids and the driver's log line: the driver's answers and refusals do not change.
Harness contrast, lint defects and the contrast formula: no contrast reading or lint check is changed.
Handler coverage and its limits, listener reading from the vdom walk: event handling is not touched.
Committed recorded checks, their recording script and byte-equality to the recording: no recorded check is added or re-recorded.
Virtual clock, advance, settle and timer-tick rows: the chunk changes no time or settle behaviour.
Mocking discipline and network stand-ins: the chunk adds no stand-in and touches no provider.
CI action pinning, secrets, read-only permissions, cache saving and trigger branches: the chunk edits no CI workflow.
Mutation testing and the cognitive-complexity ceiling on the dev host: not part of the move's measurement.
Password masking, typed-password and select-row colour rows: no form-control behaviour is in scope.
